new_today.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
new_today.title_zh: AResKGLM：一种图接地语言模型框架，用于可解释的多跳抗菌素耐药性推理。
new_today.summary_zh: 抗菌素耐药性（AMR）威胁着微生物学和微生物组生物信息学，因为耐药表型由基因、移动遗传元件和跨微生物群落的功能环境之间的相互作用塑造。优先考虑耐药决定因素需要模型在连接基因、蛋白质、通路、药物和微生物表型的知识图谱（KG）上进行推理。现有的基于图的方法将这些证据压缩为标量分数，而大型语言模型可以产生不基于结构化证据的解释。我们开发了 AResKGLM（抗菌素耐药性知识图谱语言模型），一种图接地语言模型框架，用于可解释的微生物 AMR 生物信息学，它将广度优先搜索检索的多跳路径和每个实体的生物医学描述序列化为结构化的上下文-路径-问题提示。Llama-3-8B 和 DeepSeek-R1-7B 使用 QLoRA 进行适配，以产生二元链接预测和简洁的推理轨迹。在 KIDs 基准上，AResKGLM（Llama-3-8B）实现了 F1 = 0.8482，优于 KG-BERT（0.7213）、NB

extra.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial Resistance Knowledge Graph Language Model), a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable microbial AMR bioinformatics that serializes breadth-first-search-retrieved multi-hop paths and per-entity biomedical descriptions into a structured Context-Path-Question prompt. Llama-3-8B and DeepSeek-R1-7B are adapted with QLoRA to produce binary link predictions and concise reasoning traces. On the KIDs benchmark, AResKGLM (Llama-3-8B) achieved F1 = 0.8482, outperforming KG-BERT (0.7213), NBFNet (0.5260), and ULTRA (0.2541) (paired Wilcoxon $p = 1.2 \times 10^{-7}$). Its advantage increased with reasoning depth: F1 decreased from 0.9197 at 2 hops to 0.8148 at 6 hops, whereas KG-BERT dropped from 0.8110 to 0.6716. Counterfactual path corruption produced an apparent F1 of 0.000, mechanically forced by the probe label assignment; the operative diagnostic is the per-sample flip rate (0.04-0.16), consistent with sensitivity to supplied biological evidence rather than reliance on pretrained priors alone. Cross-species evaluation yielded F1 = 0.81-0.88 with Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) = 0.35-0.54 on Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus. Temporal ranking of 81 post-2022 gene-drug associations achieved Precision@20 = 100% and AUC-PR = 0.855. AResKGLM offers an interpretable, reproducible framework for multi-hop AMR reasoning, linking candidate prioritization with mechanism-oriented hypothesis generation.

dropped.title: Topologically-based parameter inference for agent-based model selection from spatiotemporal cellular data
dropped.title_zh: 基于拓扑的参数推断用于时空细胞数据的基于代理模型选择
dropped.summary_zh: 时空单细胞成像的进展使得详细观察细胞群体动态和细胞间相互作用成为可能。然而，将这些丰富数据集转化为机制洞察仍是重大挑战。基于代理模型（ABMs）是一种自下而上的计算框架，用于研究由单个相邻细胞间相互作用规则产生的细胞群体涌现行为，而拓扑数据分析（TDA）提供空间组织的稳健描述符。我们提出TOPAZ（基于拓扑的参数推断用于基于代理模型优化），一个将TDA与近似贝叶斯计算（ABC）、近似近似贝叶斯计算（AABC）和贝叶斯模型选择相结合的计算流程，从时空细胞数据中识别生物学合理的ABMs。TOPAZ使用持续同调量化细胞轨迹的空间特征，并通过ABC和AABC结合拓扑信息进行参数推断，使用贝叶斯信息准则进行模型比较。我们使用成纤维细胞集体运动模拟验证TOPAZ，展示其准确恢复模型参数并区分基线ABM和包含对齐相互作用的扩展模型的能力。我们的结果和开源代码展示了TOPAZ作为空间单细胞分析中机制推断和

extra.description: Advances in spatiotemporal single-cell imaging have enabled detailed observations of cell population dynamics and intercellular interactions. However, translating these rich data sets into mechanistic insight remains a significant challenge. Agent-based models (ABMs) are a bottom-up computational framework for investigating the emergent behavior of cell populations that can arise from rules defining the interactions between individual neighboring cells, while topological data analysis (TDA) provides robust descriptors of spatial organization. We present TOPAZ (TOpologically-based Parameter inference for Agent-based model optimiZation), a computational pipeline that integrates TDA with approximate Bayesian computation (ABC), approximate approximate Bayesian computation (AABC), and Bayesian model selection to identify biologically plausible ABMs from spatiotemporal cellular data. TOPAZ uses persistent homology to quantify spatial features of cell trajectories and combines this topological information with parameter inference via ABC and AABC and model comparison using the Bayesian information criterion. We validate TOPAZ using simulations of collective fibroblast movement, demonstrating its ability to accurately recover model parameters and distinguish between a baseline ABM and an extended model that incorporates an alignment interaction. Our results and open-source code demonstrate the utility of TOPAZ as an extensible framework for mechanistic inference and model discrimination in spatial single-cell analysis.
